narrativeContexts.context: Identify High-Value Automation Opportunities. Analyze current manual operations identifying repetitive tasks consuming significant operational time. Review incident tickets, change requests, and operational runbooks quantifying frequency (daily, weekly, monthly) and average duration per execution. Prioritize opportunities with high frequency and duration combination (10+ weekly executions at 30+ minutes each yield 5+ hours weekly savings).

Quantify Costs and Benefits. Calculate automation development cost including developer hours for playbook authoring, testing, and job template configuration. Estimate ongoing maintenance effort (updates, bug fixes). Calculate operational savings multiplying eliminated manual execution time by hourly labor cost. Include secondary benefits: reduced human error (incident reduction), faster deployment (revenue enablement), improved compliance (audit cost reduction).

Build Business Case with ROI Projections. Document investment required (development hours, infrastructure, training) and benefits timeline (one-time benefits, recurring savings). Calculate payback period (months until cumulative savings exceed investment) and 3-year ROI. Present business case emphasizing strategic benefits beyond cost savings: deployment velocity, consistency, scalability, compliance.
Business case documented with quantified costs, benefits, ROI calculation, and stakeholder approval obtained for automation investment.

activities.name: Justify Automation Investment
activities.description: Analyzing operational manual effort and building business cases demonstrating automation ROI through deployment velocity improvements and error reduction.

narrativeContexts.context: Document Desired Automation Outcomes. Define what the automation must accomplish including target system desired state, configuration parameters, orchestration sequence, or remediation actions. Identify systems receiving automation (operating systems, versions, cloud providers, network devices, applications) and scale (number of targets, concurrent execution requirements).

Specify Non-Functional Requirements. Document idempotency requirements (must be safe for repeated execution), execution time targets (acceptable duration for user experience), credential requirements (SSH keys, API tokens, vault passwords), inventory scope (target groups, dynamic inventory sources), and execution environment dependencies (Python packages, Ansible collections).

Define Acceptance Criteria and Testing Approach. Establish testable acceptance criteria including functional validation (automation achieves desired outcomes), quality validation (ansible-lint passes, test coverage thresholds), and operational validation (job template deployed, documentation published). Plan testing approach including test targets, test scenarios, and validation procedures.
Automation requirements documented with desired outcomes, target specifications, non-functional requirements, and acceptance criteria defined.

activities.name: Define Automation Requirements
activities.description: Capturing automation functional requirements, target system specifications, credential requirements, and acceptance criteria guiding playbook design and development.

narrativeContexts.context: Create Playbook Scaffolding. Initialize playbook YAML file with descriptive name (deploy-web-server.yml). Define play with name, hosts pattern targeting inventory groups, and become directive for privilege escalation if required. Add initial tasks implementing core automation logic using appropriate Ansible modules (ansible.builtin.package, ansible.builtin.service, ansible.builtin.template).

Add Variable Parameterization. Replace hardcoded values with variables enabling customization. Define variables in vars section or separate variable files. Provide defaults using default filter or separate defaults file. Use Jinja2 templating for dynamic values. Document expected variables including types, acceptable values, and defaults.

Implement Error Handling. Add failed_when conditionals controlling failure detection. Implement block/rescue/always patterns for critical operations requiring error handling. Add meaningful task names enabling troubleshooting. Include validation tasks confirming desired outcomes achieved before proceeding with dependent tasks.

Test Locally with ansible-navigator. Execute playbook using ansible-navigator run playbook.yml against test inventory. Configure ansible-navigator.yml specifying execution environment, mode (interactive vs stdout), and logging preferences. Validate ansible-lint passes without errors. Execute in check mode (--check) validating idempotency. Run twice against same targets confirming "changed=0" on second execution.

Optimize Performance. Add tags enabling selective execution (deploy, rollback, validation). Configure async execution for long-running tasks. Optimize loops with appropriate iteration strategies. Configure fact caching reducing overhead. Set appropriate forks parallelization balancing speed and target system capacity.
Playbook executes successfully via ansible-navigator, demonstrates idempotent behavior, passes ansible-lint validation, and achieves functional requirements.

activities.name: Develop Playbooks
activities.description: Creating executable automation YAML files with plays, tasks, variable management, error handling, and idempotency validation using ansible-navigator local testing.

narrativeContexts.context: Initialize Role Structure. Execute ansible-galaxy role init role-name creating standardized directory structure (tasks, handlers, templates, files, vars, defaults, meta). Populate meta/main.yml with role metadata (author, description, license, dependencies). Create README documenting role purpose, variables, and example usage.

Implement Role Tasks and Handlers. Develop task logic in tasks/main.yml achieving role objective. Define handlers in handlers/main.yml for service restarts or configuration reloads. Create Jinja2 templates in templates/ for configuration files. Document all role variables in defaults/main.yml with defaults and type information.

Test Role with Molecule. Initialize molecule testing with molecule init scenario creating test scenario. Configure molecule.yml defining platforms (Docker containers or VMs) and test sequence. Implement test playbook in molecule/default/converge.yml. Execute molecule test running full test sequence (dependency, create, converge, idempotence, verify, destroy). Add verification tasks in molecule/default/verify.yml validating role outcomes.
Role implements functional requirements, molecule tests pass including idempotency validation, and role documentation complete.

activities.name: Create Roles
activities.description: Developing reusable automation components with standardized directory structure, task organization, variable defaults, templates, and handlers enabling composition into playbooks.

narrativeContexts.context: Initialize Collection Structure. Execute ansible-galaxy collection init namespace.name creating collection directory structure. Populate galaxy.yml with namespace, name, version (0.1.0), description, authors, license, and dependencies. Create README and CHANGELOG. Configure .gitignore excluding build artifacts.

Develop Collection Components. Add roles to roles/ directory with full role structure. Develop custom modules in plugins/modules/ implementing collection-specific functionality with ansible-doc compatible documentation. Create plugins in plugins/module_utils/, plugins/filter/, plugins/lookup/ as needed. Add example playbooks in examples/ demonstrating collection usage.

Execute ansible-test Quality Validation. Run ansible-test sanity validating Python code quality, documentation format, and import statements. Implement unit tests in tests/unit/ validating module logic. Execute ansible-test units running unit test suite. Create integration tests in tests/integration/ validating components against live systems. Run ansible-test integration executing integration test suite.

Version and Build Collection. Assign semantic version in galaxy.yml following MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH convention. Update CHANGELOG documenting changes, additions, and breaking changes. Execute ansible-galaxy collection build creating namespace-name-version.tar.gz tarball. Verify tarball contents including all roles, modules, plugins, and documentation.
Collection built successfully passing ansible-test validation, components functional, documentation complete, and tarball ready for publication.

activities.name: Author Collections
activities.description: Creating packaged Ansible content with galaxy.

narrativeContexts.context: Create Basic Job Template. Navigate to automation controller Resources → Templates → Add Job Template. Configure descriptive name and description. Select Project and Playbook from synchronized project. Assign Inventory or Smart Inventory. Configure job type (Run, Check, Scan). Set verbosity, privilege escalation, and timeout settings.

Design Survey for Parameterization. Enable survey in template configuration. Add survey questions with appropriate types (Text, Textarea, Password, Multiple Choice, Integer, Float). Configure question names (survey variable names), prompts, defaults, and validation (required, regex patterns, min/max values). Add help text explaining parameter purpose and acceptable values. Test survey via template launch UI confirming validation functions correctly.

Assign Credentials and Execution Environment. Add required credentials (Machine credential for SSH, Vault credential for encrypted variables, Cloud credentials for provider APIs). Select execution environment matching playbook dependencies. Configure credential injection ensuring playbook receives credentials without exposing values. Verify execution environment contains required collections and Python packages.

Execute Trial Run and Validate. Launch template against test inventory with survey parameter combinations. Monitor execution logs confirming expected outcomes. Validate error handling by testing failure scenarios. Confirm execution duration acceptable for user experience. Document any limitations or known issues.
Job template successfully executes playbook with expected outcomes, survey captures required parameters, credentials function correctly, and template documented.

activities.name: Define Job Templates
activities.description: Configuring automation controller job templates with playbook selection, inventory assignment, credential mapping, survey design, and execution environment selection enabling operational automation execution.

narrativeContexts.context: Design Workflow Structure. Create workflow template in automation controller. Use workflow visualizer adding nodes (job templates, project syncs, inventory updates). Define execution flow connecting nodes with edges (success, failure, always). Create workflow-level survey if runtime parameters required. Design logical flow from initiation through completion including error paths.

Configure Job Association and Variable Passing. Assign job templates to workflow nodes. Configure node options (limit patterns, tags, extra variables). Enable inventory propagation ensuring consistent inventory across workflow steps. Configure extra variables passing data from workflow to child templates and between nodes. Validate variable scoping and precedence.

Implement Branching Logic and Approvals. Connect nodes with success edges for happy path. Add failure edges implementing error handling, rollback, or notification. Configure always-run edges for cleanup or notification nodes. Add approval nodes at governance gates assigning approvers with appropriate permissions. Configure approval timeout and escalation settings.

Test and Optimize Performance. Execute workflow end-to-end validating success path. Test failure paths with intentional errors confirming error handling works correctly. Test approval flow confirming approvers receive notifications. Identify independent workflow steps configurable for parallel execution. Configure parallelization reducing total workflow duration. Validate optimization doesn't introduce race conditions.
Workflow executes successfully through all paths, approval gates function correctly, parallelization optimized, and execution duration acceptable.

activities.name: Orchestrate Workflows
activities.description: Designing multi-job orchestrations using automation controller workflow visualizer with conditional branching, approval nodes, inventory propagation, and parallel execution optimization.

narrativeContexts.context: Define Execution Environment Requirements. Create execution-environment.yml file specifying base image (quay.io/ansible/ansible-runner or ansible-ee-minimal). Document Python package requirements in requirements.txt with version constraints. List system package dependencies in bindep.txt using package manager syntax. Specify Ansible collection requirements in requirements.yml with version constraints.

Build Container Image. Execute ansible-builder build creating container image from definition. Review build logs confirming all dependencies installed without errors. Tag built image with descriptive name and version. Test build reproducibility ensuring consistent results. Configure build automation in CI/CD pipeline enabling automated rebuilds on definition changes.

Test and Optimize. Execute representative playbooks within execution environment using ansible-navigator --execution-environment image-name validating functionality. Confirm all required collections import successfully. Validate custom modules function correctly. Optimize image size removing unnecessary packages, cleaning cache, and employing multi-stage builds. Scan image for vulnerabilities remediating findings.

Publish to Registry. Push image to organizational container registry (automation hub, Quay, Harbor). Tag with semantic version and latest tag. Configure pull credentials distributing to automation controller and developers. Document image purpose, dependencies, and usage. Establish lifecycle management including versioning, deprecation, and update procedures.
Execution environment built successfully, playbooks execute correctly within environment, image published to registry, and documentation complete.

activities.name: Build Execution Environments
activities.description: Creating custom container images with execution-environment.

narrativeContexts.context: Configure Syntax Validation. Create .ansible-lint configuration file defining organizational linting rules. Execute ansible-lint against playbooks validating YAML syntax, Jinja2 templates, deprecated module avoidance, and best practices. Configure ansible-lint in CI/CD pipeline gating pull request merges. Address lint findings iteratively improving code quality.

Implement Unit Tests. For roles, initialize molecule testing with molecule init. Configure molecule scenarios testing default configuration and parameter variations. For collections, create unit tests in tests/unit/ validating module logic in isolation. Execute ansible-test units running unit test suite. Establish test coverage baseline tracking improvement over time.

Create Integration Tests. Implement molecule integration tests validating roles against test containers or VMs. Create ansible-test integration tests in tests/integration/ validating collections against live systems. Test multiple platform variations (OS versions, cloud providers). Include error scenario testing validating graceful failure handling.

Automate Testing in CI/CD. Integrate all testing (lint, units, integration) into CI/CD pipeline. Configure automated test execution on pull requests. Set quality gates requiring test passage before merge. Configure test result reporting and coverage tracking. Optimize test execution time through parallelization and caching.
Test suite implements syntax validation, unit tests, and integration tests with CI/CD automation and quality gates enforced.

activities.name: Test Automation
activities.description: Implementing automated testing frameworks with ansible-lint syntax validation, molecule role testing, and ansible-test collection testing ensuring automation quality before production deployment.

narrativeContexts.context: Assign Semantic Version. Update galaxy.yml version field following MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH convention (breaking changes increment MAJOR, new features increment MINOR, bug fixes increment PATCH). Update CHANGELOG documenting changes, additions, deprecations, and breaking changes. Create Git tag matching version (v1.2.3) enabling version-specific checkout.

Build Collection Tarball. Execute ansible-galaxy collection build creating namespace-name-version.tar.gz. Verify tarball contents extracting and reviewing (all roles, modules, plugins, galaxy.yml, README, LICENSE). Configure build_ignore in galaxy.yml excluding development files (.git, tests, molecule). Validate build reproducibility.

Manage Build Artifacts. Store build artifacts with version information in artifact repository or version control releases. Configure automated builds in CI/CD pipeline triggered by version tags. Maintain build history enabling rollback to previous versions. Document build procedure and artifact locations.
Collection tarball built successfully with proper versioning, contents verified, build process documented, and artifacts managed.

activities.name: Package Content
activities.description: Building Ansible collection tarballs with ansible-galaxy collection build, semantic versioning, dependency declaration, and build artifact management preparing content for distribution.

narrativeContexts.context: Upload Collection to Automation Hub. Authenticate to private automation hub obtaining API token. Execute ansible-galaxy collection publish tarball --server=hub-url --token=token uploading collection. Alternatively, use automation hub UI Upload Collection feature. Verify collection appears in automation hub with correct metadata.

Obtain Namespace Approval. Request namespace approval from automation hub administrators if first publication to namespace. Provide namespace justification (organizational unit, domain, team). Configure namespace ownership assigning appropriate team members. Document namespace governance (who can publish, approval requirements).

Validate Collection Consumption. Test collection installation using ansible-galaxy collection install namespace.name verifying download succeeds. Execute example playbooks confirming collection functionality. Validate dependency resolution if collection depends on other collections. Create automation controller project referencing collection in requirements.yml validating project synchronization.

Communicate Availability and Support. Announce collection availability to development teams via communication channels. Publish collection documentation in organization knowledge base. Establish support process (issue tracking, contact information, SLA). Track collection usage metrics (downloads, projects using collection).
Collection published to automation hub, namespace approved, consumption validated, and availability communicated.

activities.name: Distribute Content
activities.description: Publishing Ansible collections to private automation hub with namespace approval, signature verification, and consumption validation enabling organizational content sharing and reuse.

narrativeContexts.context: Generate and Secure GPG Keys. Generate organizational GPG key pair using gpg --full-generate-key with appropriate key type and expiration. Secure private key with strong passphrase and restricted file permissions. Export public key using gpg --export --armor distributing to automation hub and developers. Document key management policy (creation, rotation, revocation).

Sign Content with ansible-sign. Execute ansible-sign project gpg-sign project-directory --gpg-key key-id creating detached signatures. For collections, sign tarball using ansible-sign collection sign namespace-name-version.tar.gz. Verify signature created successfully and accompanies content artifact. Document signing procedure.

Automate Signing in CI/CD. Configure CI/CD pipeline to execute ansible-sign automatically on builds. Store GPG private key securely in CI/CD secrets management. Configure pipeline to sign only successful builds passing quality gates. Distribute signatures alongside content artifacts.

Configure Signature Verification. Configure private automation hub to verify signatures on collection uploads. Distribute public key to automation hub enabling verification. Test signature verification uploading signed collection. Configure enforcement rejecting unsigned content if organizational policy requires.
Content signing operational with GPG keys managed securely, automated signing in CI/CD, and signature verification configured in automation hub.

activities.name: Sign Content
activities.description: Applying GPG digital signatures to automation content using ansible-sign for supply chain security and provenance verification supporting compliance requirements.

narrativeContexts.context: Configure Source Control Integration. Configure Git repository webhook triggering CI/CD pipeline on pull request creation and branch merges. Define branch protection rules requiring pipeline success before merge. Configure pipeline to clone repository, checkout appropriate branch, and initialize execution environment.

Implement Automated Quality Gates. Configure pipeline stage executing ansible-lint validation failing on errors. Add stage running ansible-test sanity for collections. Execute molecule tests for roles or ansible-test units for collections. Configure integration testing against test infrastructure. Set test coverage thresholds gating pipeline progression.

Automate Content Signing and Publication. Add pipeline stage building collection tarball on successful test completion. Execute ansible-sign creating content signatures. Configure automated publication to automation hub for main branch merges. Tag Git repository with semantic version triggering release pipeline.

Implement Pipeline Notifications and Monitoring. Configure pipeline notifications on success, failure, or approval requirements. Integrate with communication platforms (Slack, Microsoft Teams) alerting on pipeline events. Track pipeline metrics (success rate, duration, frequency). Optimize pipeline execution time through caching and parallelization.
CI/CD pipeline operational with automated testing, signing, and publication triggered by source control events.

activities.name: Integrate CI/CD
activities.description: Configuring automated pipelines with source control webhook triggers, ansible-lint validation, ansible-test execution, content signing, and automated publication enabling continuous delivery of automation content.

narrativeContexts.context: Design User-Friendly Survey. Create survey questions with clear prompts explaining parameter purpose. Add comprehensive help text with examples and acceptable values. Provide sensible defaults for common scenarios. Configure validation preventing invalid input (required fields, regex patterns, min/max values). Test survey usability with representative end users gathering feedback.

Create Operational Documentation. Write user guide explaining template purpose, expected outcomes, and execution time. Document survey parameters with detailed descriptions and examples. Create troubleshooting section addressing common issues. Publish documentation in organization knowledge base or automation catalog. Include contact information for support escalation.

Configure RBAC and Approvals. Grant Execute permission to appropriate teams based on business requirements. Configure approval workflow for sensitive operations requiring management review. Set approval timeout and escalation procedures. Test approval flow confirming approvers receive notifications and approvals gate execution. Document approval requirements and criteria.

Monitor Usage and Iterate. Track template execution metrics (frequency, success rate, users). Collect user feedback through surveys or support channel. Analyze common failure patterns addressing issues. Iterate template design based on analytics and feedback improving usability. Maintain version history documenting improvements.
Self-service template published with user-friendly survey, comprehensive documentation, RBAC configured, and usage monitoring operational.

activities.name: Create Self-Service Templates
activities.description: Designing job templates for end-user consumption with comprehensive survey help text, operational documentation, RBAC configuration, and approval workflows enabling business-driven automation.

narrativeContexts.context: Configure Lightspeed Integration. Install Ansible VS Code extension with Lightspeed support. Authenticate to Red Hat Ansible Lightspeed service obtaining access. Configure organizational content model integration if available enabling context-aware suggestions. Validate Lightspeed functional by testing simple playbook generation.

Generate Playbook Scaffolding. Describe desired automation outcome in natural language comment (# Install and configure nginx web server with SSL). Accept Lightspeed-generated playbook structure including plays, hosts, and initial tasks. Review generated code validating modules, parameters, and logic appropriateness. Refine prompts iteratively improving generated code quality.

Use Task-Level Suggestions. Begin typing task name receiving Lightspeed module recommendations. Accept suggestions accelerating task authoring. Use Lightspeed for Jinja2 template generation. Leverage AI-generated variable management patterns. Validate all AI-generated code reviewing for security issues, deprecated modules, or logic errors.

Refine and Test Generated Content. Execute generated playbook against test targets validating functionality. Add error handling, idempotency improvements, and variable parameterization not generated by AI. Run ansible-lint addressing any issues. Document which portions were AI-generated for future reference.
Lightspeed integrated in development workflow, playbooks generated successfully with AI assistance, and generated code validated for quality and security.

activities.name: Use Lightspeed AI
activities.description: Leveraging Red Hat Ansible Lightspeed with IBM watsonx Code Assistant for AI-powered playbook generation, task suggestions, and module recommendations accelerating content development.

narrativeContexts.context: Install Development Tools. Install IDE (VS Code, PyCharm, or provision Red Hat Developer Hub workspace). Install Ansible core or ansible-dev-tools package providing ansible-navigator and related tools. Install container runtime (podman or docker) enabling execution environment usage. Configure source control with Git installation and SSH key generation.

Configure ansible-navigator and ansible.cfg. Create ansible-navigator.yml defining execution environment preferences, mode (interactive vs stdout), and logging configuration. Create ansible.cfg configuring inventory paths, role paths, collection paths, and defaults. Install Ansible VS Code extension enabling syntax highlighting, linting integration, and Lightspeed AI. Configure ansible-lint with organizational rules.

Integrate with Automation Controller. Configure automation controller access in ansible-navigator enabling job template testing. Obtain API token for authentication. Clone relevant Git repositories providing access to playbooks and collections under development. Configure project synchronization testing local changes in automation controller projects.

Prepare Execution Environments. Pull base execution environment images from automation hub (ansible-ee-minimal, ansible-ee-supported). Pull or build custom execution environments required for team automation. Configure ansible-navigator default execution environment. Validate playbook execution within execution environments confirming functionality.
Development workspace operational with ansible-navigator configured, automation controller integrated, execution environments available, and tooling functional.

activities.name: Provision Development Workspace
activities.description: Setting up automation development environments with ansible-navigator, VS Code extension, execution environment configuration, and automation controller connectivity enabling productive content authoring.

narrativeContexts.context: Capture and Prioritize Work Items. Create work items in backlog system (Jira, Azure DevOps, GitHub Issues) for automation development tasks. Classify work items (playbook development, collection authoring, job template configuration, workflow design). Document initial requirements and acceptance criteria. Prioritize based on business value, dependencies, and risk reduction. Assign preliminary team or persona responsible.

Refine Work Items in Backlog Grooming. Conduct regular backlog grooming sessions refining work item details. Decompose large initiatives into manageable tasks. Estimate complexity using story points accounting for development, testing, and deployment effort. Identify and document dependencies on other work items or infrastructure. Define explicit testable acceptance criteria.

Plan Sprint/Iteration Work. Conduct sprint planning selecting work items for upcoming sprint based on team capacity and priorities. Assign work items to automation developers, DevOps engineers, or collection maintainers. Establish sprint goals and success criteria. Communicate sprint commitments to stakeholders.

Track Progress and Close Work Items. Update work item status regularly (daily standups, kanban board moves). Mark work in progress, under review, or blocked as appropriate. Complete work items when acceptance criteria met, pull requests merged, and artifacts published. Conduct retrospectives capturing lessons learned and process improvements. Groom follow-up work items identified during development.
Automation backlog organized, work items refined with acceptance criteria, sprint planning operational, and work completion tracked.

activities.name: Manage Automation Backlog
activities.description: Organizing automation development work items with backlog grooming, sprint planning, task tracking, and completion validation enabling predictable automation delivery.

alphas.name: Automation Content

states.name: Authored
states.description: Initial automation content created with basic structure and functional logic.

checklist.name: Content Repository Created
checklist.description: Automation content resides in version-controlled Git repository with appropriate directory structure (playbook project, role skeleton, or collection layout from ansible-galaxy init).

checklist.name: Functional Logic Implemented
checklist.description: Content implements intended purpose with playbook tasks, role tasks, or collection modules/plugins performing desired configuration management or orchestration.

checklist.name: Basic Error Handling Present
checklist.description: Content includes fundamental error handling with failed_when conditions, block/rescue/always patterns, and meaningful task names.

checklist.name: Execution Environment Dependencies Identified
checklist.description: Required Python packages, system libraries, and Ansible collections documented with version constraints.

checklist.name: Initial Commit Recorded
checklist.description: Content committed to source control with meaningful commit message describing automation purpose and implementation approach.

states.name: Validated
states.description: Automation content passes syntax validation and best practice checks.

checklist.name: Ansible-Lint Validation Passed
checklist.description: Content executes through ansible-lint without errors, confirming YAML syntax, Jinja2 validity, deprecated module avoidance, and best practice compliance.

checklist.name: YAML Syntax Verified
checklist.description: All YAML files parse correctly with consistent indentation, proper list/dictionary formatting, and valid Jinja2 template expressions.

checklist.name: Variable Naming Standards Applied
checklist.description: Variable names follow organizational conventions (snake_case, descriptive names, namespacing), use defaults appropriately, and document expected values and types.

checklist.name: Deprecation Warnings Addressed
checklist.description: Content avoids deprecated Ansible modules, keywords, or patterns, utilizing current recommended approaches.

checklist.name: Documentation Standards Met
checklist.description: Content includes required documentation (README describing purpose and usage, variables documented with types and defaults, example playbooks).

states.name: Tested
states.description: Automation content validated through automated testing frameworks.

checklist.name: Unit Tests Implemented
checklist.description: Role testing with molecule or collection unit tests with ansible-test units validate component behavior in isolation.

checklist.name: Integration Tests Executed
checklist.description: End-to-end tests validate content against representative target systems confirming desired outcomes achieved.

checklist.name: Check Mode Validation Passed
checklist.description: Playbooks execute successfully in check mode (--check flag) predicting changes without applying them, confirming idempotency design.

checklist.name: Multi-Platform Testing Completed
checklist.description: Content tested against all target platform variations (OS versions, cloud providers, device types) confirming compatibility.

checklist.name: Test Coverage Threshold Met
checklist.description: Automated tests achieve organizational coverage thresholds (typically 70-80% for roles, comprehensive sanity for collections).

states.name: Packaged
states.description: Automation content organized, versioned, and ready for distribution.

checklist.name: Collection Structure Finalized
checklist.description: Collections follow ansible-galaxy structure with galaxy.yml metadata, proper role/module/plugin organization, and namespace conventions.

checklist.name: Semantic Version Assigned
checklist.description: Content tagged with semantic version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) following organizational versioning strategy.

checklist.name: Dependencies Declared
checklist.description: Collection dependencies listed in galaxy.yml, role dependencies in meta/main.yml, and execution environment dependencies in requirements files.

checklist.name: Build Artifacts Created
checklist.description: Collections built into tarball artifacts (namespace-name-version.tar.gz), playbooks organized in project repositories.

checklist.name: Build Process Documented
checklist.description: Collection build procedure documented including ansible-galaxy collection build commands and build pipeline integration.

states.name: Signed

checklist.name: GPG Signing Key Configured
checklist.description: Organizational or team GPG key pair created with private key secured and public key distributed for verification.

checklist.name: Ansible-Sign Executed
checklist.description: Content signed using ansible-sign CLI creating detached signature files accompanying collection tarballs or project commits.

checklist.name: Signature Verification Validated
checklist.description: Signed content verified using public key confirming signature validity and content integrity.

checklist.name: Signing Integrated in CI/CD
checklist.description: Automated signing incorporated into build pipeline ensuring all released content receives signature.

checklist.name: Signature Policy Documented
checklist.description: Content signing policy documented including which content requires signatures, key management procedures, and verification requirements.

states.name: Published

checklist.name: Content Uploaded to Automation Hub
checklist.description: Collections uploaded to private automation hub or playbooks synchronized to automation controller projects.

checklist.name: Namespace Approval Obtained
checklist.description: Collection namespace approved by automation hub administrators with appropriate ownership and access controls.

checklist.name: Content Searchable
checklist.description: Published content appears in automation hub search results with complete metadata (description, tags, version, dependencies).

checklist.name: Dependencies Resolvable
checklist.description: All content dependencies available in automation hub or linked remote repositories enabling successful dependency resolution.

checklist.name: Download Verification Validated
checklist.description: Content successfully downloadable and installable by automation developers and automation controller projects.

states.name: Certified
states.description: Automation content approved for production use with governance validation complete.

checklist.name: Security Scan Completed

checklist.name: Compliance Validation Passed
checklist.description: Content validated against organizational compliance requirements (naming conventions, documentation standards, testing thresholds).

checklist.name: Production Approval Granted
